text:
In 2000, Blockbuster could have bought Netflix for just $50 million, and its CEO famously struggled not to laugh. Today Netflix is worth around $300 billion and only one Blockbuster store is left. But turning down Netflix wasn't Blockbuster's biggest mistake.

In this animated explainer you'll see how the world's biggest video-rental chain built a money machine on late fees, how it fought back against Netflix with Blockbuster Online and Total Access, how it briefly had Netflix on the ropes, and how a boardroom fight over a CEO bonus threw that comeback away.

What you'll learn:
• Why Blockbuster said no to buying Netflix for $50 million in 2000
• How late fees made Blockbuster around $800 million in a single year
• How Total Access let Blockbuster beat Netflix at its own game
• Why Netflix lost subscribers in 2007
• How Carl Icahn, a CEO bonus and a new strategy changed Blockbuster's fate
• Why Blockbuster went bankrupt in 2010, and the lesson for every company facing disruption
